title: Head Spins When He Stands

patient.name: Mr Abdullah bin Hassan
patient.presenting_complaint: Feeling giddy when standing up; has just been dilated for a fundus examination

history.hpc: Mr Abdullah was dilated about 25 minutes ago for a fundus check. While waiting, he tells you he feels giddy whenever he stands up quickly. He says: 'When I stand up fast, my head spin spin, like want to fall, must hold the chair first.' His near vision is now blurry and he is light-sensitive from the dilation. He has not eaten much today.
history.pmhx: Hypertension on multiple medications. Type 2 diabetes. Background diabetic retinopathy under monitoring.
history.social_hx: Lives with wife. Came by himself today on the bus. Skipped breakfast before coming.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Pupils well dilated bilaterally; otherwise normal
examination_findings.fundus: Background diabetic retinopathy, for doctor review now that pupils are dilated

investigations.fall_risk_assessment: High risk: postural (orthostatic) dizziness on standing, on multiple blood-pressure-lowering medications and a diuretic, skipped a meal (possible low blood sugar), post-dilation blurring and photosensitivity, and currently unaccompanied.
investigations.va_distance: RE and LE 6/12 pre-dilation, both now blurred post-dilation.

diagnosis: High fall risk from postural dizziness, likely contributed to by his antihypertensives/diuretic and skipped meal, compounded by acute post-dilation visual blurring. The systemic contributors and the dilation together make standing and walking hazardous right now.

immediate: Recognise the postural dizziness as a significant fall risk and do not let the patient stand or walk unaided right now
Advise him to stand up slowly in stages (sit, pause, then stand with support) rather than quickly
Seat him safely in a supervised area and stay with or observe him while symptoms settle
Inform the nurse-in-charge about the dizziness and that he skipped a meal, so blood pressure/sugar can be reviewed if needed
Offer sunglasses/UV protectors for post-dilation photosensitivity
Document the fall risk assessment, the contributing factors, and the actions taken
follow_up: Doctor/nurse to assess the postural dizziness (e.g., blood pressure, blood sugar) before he leaves
Doctor to proceed with the dilated fundus examination once he is stable
Ensure he is escorted out and advise attending with a companion in future
patient_education: Explain that standing up too fast and his medications can make him giddy, and to rise slowly in stages
Advise him not to skip meals before clinic visits
Explain the post-dilation blurring and light sensitivity will last 4-6 hours
Advise him to ask for help before walking and to come with a companion next time

key_points: Elicits the postural nature of the dizziness (worse on standing quickly)
Identifies the multiple antihypertensives and diuretic as possible contributors
Notes the skipped meal as a possible low-blood-sugar contributor
Recognises post-dilation blurring and photosensitivity as added acute risks
Performs and documents a fall risk assessment at this visit
Identifies the combination of systemic and dilation-related risk factors
Recognises the need to escalate the dizziness for review (BP/sugar)
Documents pre-dilation VA and IOP appropriately
Classifies the patient as high fall risk
Links the dizziness to medications and the skipped meal, compounded by dilation
Understands this requires active measures and escalation, not just a note
Does not dismiss the dizziness as trivial
Prevents unaided standing/walking and advises slow staged rising
Seats him safely under supervision and escalates to the nurse-in-charge
Offers practical measures (sunglasses) and documents the assessment and actions
Provides clear education on medications, meals, and post-dilation safety
